subtopic: Chromosomes and transmission of hereditary characters

lesson.title: DNA, genes and chromosomes
lesson.body: Traits such as height and blood group are passed from parents to children. The instructions are carried by DNA in the nucleus. DNA is coiled into structures called chromosomes, and a gene is a short section of DNA that controls a trait. A human body cell has 46 chromosomes, in 23 pairs. Gametes (sperm and egg) are made by meiosis, which halves the number of chromosomes to 23. During meiosis the two genes of a pair separate, so each gamete carries only one. This is called segregation. At fertilization a sperm and an egg join and the number returns to 46. The gametes meet by chance, so the new combination of genes is random.
lesson.audio_script: Traits are passed from parents to children by genes. Genes are sections of DNA, and DNA is packed into chromosomes in the nucleus. A human body cell has forty-six chromosomes. Gametes are made by meiosis and have twenty-three. At fertilization, a sperm and an egg join, and the number goes back to forty-six.
